text:
Riley: hi team — planning parental leave Aug 8 for ~14 weeks. Trying to understand hiring vs internal coverage options. prefer to backfill with a temp hire if possible. any policy constraints?

Nora (People Ops): congrats! :tada: policy-wise you can request either an internal temporary transfer or an external temp hire. key differences: internal transfer needs manager approval and org-level headcount reallocation; external temp uses vendor PO and can be faster if urgent.

Ben (Hiring): For external temp we can post a 2-month contract req on our ATS. Timeline: 1) post + collect resumes (1 week), 2) 2-stage interviews (1 week), 3) offer + notice (1 week). So ~3 weeks total if we move fast.

Kai (Manager): If we can get a contractor in 3 weeks that works. If not, I'd like to explore an internal 12-week rotation from another infra team. How do we formally request a rotation?

Nora (People Ops): To request an internal rotation, file a temporary reallocation form: https://intra.redwood/hr/temp-transfer. We'll need: start/end dates, approval from source manager, and an impact note. People Ops can triage and reach out to team leads.

Riley: Are there limits to how long a contractor can be engaged under the expedited path? I'm trying to avoid lengthy vendor onboarding.

Nora (People Ops): Expedited vendor onboarding covers contractors up to 90 days. For anything >90 days we require standard vendor review which adds ~2 weeks. If you need 14 weeks that's 98 days, so it's just over the threshold — recommend splitting into 90 days + 8 days or plan for the standard path. We can also request an exception for short overages if the business case is strong.

Ben (Hiring): Another option: hire a contractor for 10 weeks and extend via an internal temp transfer for the last 4 weeks. That avoids the long vendor cycle and gives us time to line up an internal cover.

Kai (Manager): Good idea. Also two operational notes: 1) any cover that needs prod access needs justification and a 2-week knowledge transfer overlap; 2) create a short runbook for on-call coverage.

Nora (People Ops): We'll attach access rules to the transfer/contract SOW: least privilege, time-bound credentials, and scheduled credential expiration. Also People Ops will run a quick risk check for customer-data scopes.

Riley: Regarding pay/benefits — will an internal rotation keep my health premiums and accruals intact?

Nora (People Ops): Yes — if you remain an employee and take an internal rotation, benefits continue as usual. External contractors are not on our benefits and payroll handles top-ups for parental leave separately.

PayrollBot: Reminder: submit leave form 10 business days before start to avoid payroll delay. Link: https://intra.redwood/hr/forms/leave-request

Riley: Thanks. Action items: Riley to decide by May 10 if contractor + internal handoff or pure internal rotation; Ben to draft short contract req if needed; Nora to prep temp-transfer form and risk checklist.

Ben (Hiring): I'll ping candidate sourcers now and aim to have a shortlist in 5 business days.

Nora (People Ops): I'll also check with Legal about the 98-day edge case and see if we can get expedited approval.

Kai (Manager): I'll map coverage on the team calendar and propose a 10-day overlap plan.

Riley: appreciate it all — will update here once I choose the route.
